questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences into a coherent paragraph. (P) Yet the city's residents continued to complain of potholes, clogged drains and unreliable buses. (Q) Mumbai's municipal budget in 2024 was larger than the entire state budget of seven smaller states combined. (R) The gap between expenditure and delivery thus became the most telling symptom of an urban-governance crisis. (S) Clearly, money alone was not translating into civic outcomes. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q is the opening statistic. P introduces 'Yet' — setting contrast with Q. S draws the inference ('money alone was not translating'). R states the conclusion ('thus became the most telling symptom'). Argument: Fact → Counter-observation → Inference → Conclusion.

questions.stem: Arrange the sentences. (P) By the time the second monsoon arrived, the engineers were confident the dam could absorb a one-in-fifty-year flood. (Q) The first test came in July 2023, when an unexpected three-day cloudburst swelled the reservoir to 80 % capacity in 48 hours. (R) The dam was commissioned in late 2022 with much fanfare. (S) To everyone's relief, the spillway operated exactly as modelled and the water receded within a week.
questions.explanation: R introduces the dam (commissioning). Q introduces 'first test' (chronologically follows). S describes the outcome of that first test. P closes with what happened 'by the time the second monsoon arrived'. Time-marker chain: 2022 commissioning → July 2023 first test → relief → next monsoon.

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This, not any single battle, is what finally broke the empire's grip on the countryside. (Q) The colonial state had long relied on a small cadre of British officers commanding Indian troops. (R) By 1946 those very troops, having tasted Axis prison camps, returned with a changed sense of loyalty. (S) Mutinies in the Royal Indian Navy and among army personnel followed within months.
questions.explanation: Q is the setup (how the empire kept order). R introduces the break point (1946 returning troops). S shows the immediate consequence (mutinies). P delivers the verdict that this — not any single battle — was the decisive factor. Argumentative climax ordering.

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) But as treatment costs climbed, so did accusations that the plan was excluding exactly those for whom it was designed. (Q) Ayushman Bharat, launched in 2018, promised free hospital care up to ₹5 lakh for the bottom 40 % of Indian households. (R) Policy-makers responded in 2024 with a doubled cap of ₹10 lakh and the addition of day-care procedures. (S) Within its first three years, millions had availed of surgeries their families could never have afforded.
questions.explanation: Q introduces the scheme. S notes immediate success. P flips to criticism ('But'). R closes with the policy response. Structure: Scheme → early success → criticism → reform response.

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The mobile phone reached rural India not through a national campaign but through sheer market pull. (Q) Operators, led by private companies, competed aggressively on call-rate per-minute, driving the cost of voice calls to the world's lowest. (R) When a farmer in a Bihar village could reach his buyer in Kolkata for less than a rupee, the phone stopped being a luxury. (S) Between 2005 and 2015 India added nearly a billion subscribers — a scale unmatched in the history of any technology.
questions.explanation: P is the topic sentence. Q explains HOW (price war). R is the concrete illustration. S gives the scale — the consequence. Standard 'topic → mechanism → example → consequence' structure.
